answer: A shared staking registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity post a bond that is slashed on fraud. Newcomers start with low trust and earn reputation only through verified work, so an attacker spawning many fake agents must fund every one. Like jade graded by cutters, each identity is scored on its record; a gale of fresh accounts cannot outvote established ones because voting weight follows stake and history, not headcount. Basalt-strong bonds mean faking a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds, so the attack prices itself out.
